job.title: Operations Associate
job.description:
Founded in 2017, Resolve Foundation is an award-winning Section 88 charity dedicated to empowering changemakers. Our vision is to create a Hong Kong where everyone belongs and upholds inclusion. Despite being a global city, 1 in 8 people in Hong Kong report experiencing discrimination (EOC, 2021). We believe we all can be empowered to actively change this, in big and small ways.

Our mission is to amplify marginalized voices, empower diverse changemakers and build intersectional communities to elevate our collective social impact. Our values stand for Resolve: Rights, Equality, Solidarity, Organization, Leadership, Voice and Empowerment. Our organizational culture emphasizes: diversity, learning, responsibility, collaboration and gratitude. Learn more: resolvehk.org.

About the Role
The Operations Associate will serve as the operational anchor of Resolve’s daily administration, working in close coordination with and directly reporting to the Operations Director. In this capacity, you will maintain robust, efficient administrative, human resources, financial, and facility systems that keep our team supported and our organization running seamlessly. This position is an initial 12-month full time contract, with renewal subject to performance and funding

Key Job Duties
1. Internal Finance Support & Bookkeeping Assistance
● Digital Accounting System Support : Act as the primary contact point for day-to-day bookkeeping with the external accounting firm.
● Internal Helpdesk & Reimbursements: Assist team members' inquiries regarding financial workflows; guide staff accurately through spending approval and reimbursement processes.
● Petty Cash Oversight: Maintain, disburse, and thoroughly log the physical and digital office petty cash funds for minor daily expenses.
● Budgeting & Grant Tracking: Assist the Operations Director with various financial reports and grant tracking
● Audit, Procurement, & Compliance: Facilitate the procurement processes for the team. Maintain official organizational registrations, and compliance filings.

2. Human Resources Operations & Culture
● Employee Lifecycle Logistics: Administrative setups for onboarding new hires, coordinating offboarding logistics for existing staff, and keeping digital personnel files continuously secure and compliant.
● HR Metrics & Leave Tracking: Maintain comprehensive tracking of staff attendance, statutory/annual leave, and sick leave logs. Expand data maintenance to encompass general internal HR metrics.
● Employee Engagement Surveys: Administer, distribute, and collect responses for the Annual Employee Engagement Survey, helping synthesize feedback data for management.
● Payroll & Benefits Support: Accurately assemble and prepare monthly payroll sheets, Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) contribution drafts, and general benefits data for final director sign-off.
● Recruitment Coordination: Partner closely with hiring managers to post job listings, screen incoming resumes against criteria, assemble screening binders, and coordinate interview schedules.

3. Office Administration, Facilities & IT Support
● CRM System Optimization: Administer and maintain our CRM system. Actively research, map out, and propose structural workflow enhancements to elevate how our internal operations utilize CRM infrastructure.
● Front-Line IT Helpdesk: Provide basic, essential IT assistance to internal team members (including email setups, password updates, and software licensing access requests).
● Third-Party IT Liaison: Serve as the primary operational link and point of contact with our external, third-party IT support vendor to resolve technical issues quickly.

4. Internship Program Management
● Intern Recruitment: Lead talent acquisition by collaborating with institutes and organizations
● Intern Onboarding and Offboarding: Manage the complete lifecycle of the interns, including their comprehensive onboarding and formal offboarding processes.
● Intern Experience: Communicate with program line managers to ensure that every intern gains real project ownership and meaningful career development opportunities.

Essential Skills & Requirements
● Experience: Open to motivated fresh graduates demonstrating strong layout management capabilities through internships, or candidates with 1–3 years of experience in bookkeeping, administrative, HR support, or organizational operations roles. Experience within the non-profit or NGO landscape is a distinct advantage.
● Core Competencies: Exceptional organizational habits, sharp attention to detail, strict data confidentiality maintenance, and a service-oriented mindset.
● Technical Literacy: Tech-savvy profile with fluent command over cloud productivity suites (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) and foundational human resources software platforms.
● CRM and Accounting System Proficiency: Practical experience using CRM and accounting system; exposure to Odoo and Xero are highly beneficial.
● Language Fluency: Professional verbal and written proficiency in both English and Cantonese to manage local vendor transactions and partner communications.

Location
Sheung Wan, Hong Kong. Resolve allows for flexible working currently at a ratio of 40 (remote) /60 (in office).

Salary & Benefits
The expected salary for this role is $18,000 to $20,000 depending on experience. Note that Resolve has an established salary structure that is regularly reviewed against the market and set against a Competency Framework. Other benefits include flexible working and considerations for a balanced work-life relationship, health and dental insurance, opportunities for training and development, a culture of wellbeing and team-building, and above-market levels of annual leave. Resolve will provide you with a work phone and laptop. We are also based out of a larger social impact coworking space that has perks and organizes several activities and events.

Equal Opportunities
We believe a diverse and inclusive team is key to our success and social impact. We actively welcome and encourage applications from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, age, disability, religion, or belief. As one of the first 100 signatories to the Racial Diversity & Inclusion Charter of the Equal Opportunities Commission, we are proud to be building a more equitable workplace. Your unique perspective is valued here and will make our nonprofit stronger. If you need any special assistance or accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know.

Application Process
Interested candidates in the role should apply on or before October 7, 2026. Should you have any questions on the position, or need any support, please email jobs@resolvehk.org. Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted about the status of their application.

job.title: CHAIR, BOARD OF DIRECTORS
job.description:
The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong kong)

Our Purpose
We are determined to deliver Fred Hollows’ vision of preventing blindness and restoring sight.

Our priority is to work with communities to improve their own eye health. We do this through life-changing surgeries and treatments, training doctors and health workers, generating new ideas, and pushing for change at all levels – from local to global. The Foundation works in more than 25 developing in East Asia, South Asia and the Middle East, Africa and Australasia.

The Fred Hollows Foundation (“The Foundation”) established the Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) over a decade ago, and together with other international organisations in the United Kingdom, Kenya and the United States of America, the international organisations form a global network to support the work of The Foundation. The Foundation’s latest Annual Report is available here[SB1]  and the Global Strategy 2024-2028 is available here.

ROLE Purpose 
The Chair leads The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) (FHF (HK)) Board of Directors to achieve its aim: ending avoidable blindness and restoring sight to those in need.

Within the global Fred Hollows Foundation network, FHF HK plays a primary role in mobilising resources (as a ‘market entity’) to support sight-restoring work in low- and middle-income countries.

By 2030, FHF HK aspires to be The Foundation’s trusted catalyst of resourcing for the Greater China Region, unlocking resources, partnerships and influence to scale eye health equity across Asia. FHF HK will do this by serving as The Foundation’s regional philanthropy hub in Greater China, mobilising capital (donations, institutional philanthropy and investment), partnerships and influence across Hong Kong and Macau to scale eye health impact.

The Chair plays a critical role in ensuring effective governance leadership, strong strategic oversight, and alignment with The Foundation’s vision of a world in which no one is needlessly blind. The Chair also leverages their networks to unlock access to prospective significant supporters and facilitates engagement with priority stakeholders and events that would not otherwise be accessible to FHF HK.

With the term of the current Chair concluding at the end of November 2026, it is suggested that a new Chair be appointed in the lead up to the expiry of the current Chair’s term.

Role of The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) Chair
The Chair of the Board of The Fred Hollows Foundation (Hong Kong) is appointed by the Board of Directors, with Directors approved by the Global Board of the sole member (The Foundation).
The Chair serves for two three-year terms. Directors may serve a maximum of nine consecutive years. The powers of Directors, the Board and its Chair are set out in the Articles of Association and the Corporate Governance Charter.

The Chair is expected to:
  1. Ensure, in partnership with the Board, that FHF HK’s strategy is aligned with The Foundation’s Vision and Strategy, and that goals are achieved with integrity.
  2. Promote the values and goals of The Foundation in all aspects of governance and engagement with members, employees, partners, governments and communities.
  3. Perform duties in alignment with The Foundation’s Charter, the Articles of Association and relevant law, ensuring FHF HK operates in an ethically, environmentally and socially responsible manner.
  4. Lead the Board with tact and diplomacy, promoting a culture of integrity, respect, transparency, collaboration, resourcefulness and compliance.
  5. Chair Board meetings to ensure they are effective, efficient, and support high-quality, ethical decision-making.
  6. Commit sufficient time to the role, including representing FHF HK at donor, corporate, government and community engagements, and providing access to professional and philanthropic networks.
  7. Build a productive working relationship with management, including the Head of Market Hong Kong and Macau and relevant Global teams, including setting Board agendas.
  8. Engage with The Foundation’s initiatives to evolve global governance frameworks.
 
Essential Experience
  1. Demonstrated experience to Chair the Board.
  2. Demonstrated ability to implement and oversee governance, integrity and compliance processes at a board level.
  3. Demonstrated ability to lead and implement change.
  4. Demonstrated ability to develop substantial philanthropic, business or corporate fundraising networks and relationships on behalf of The Foundation and take part in high level meetings.
Desirable Experience
  1. Demonstrated experience negotiating and partnering with not-for-profits, corporations, governments, multi-lateral and other non-government agencies in pursuit of The Foundation’s goals and interests.
  2. Understanding of how a brand is perceived in the market and execution of brand management
  3. Experience working with an international health and development organisation.
  4. Demonstrated understanding of working with developing countries and human rights.
  5. An established public profile known for credible authentic leadership with access to high level decision makers in government and industry
Skills
1.    Strategic leadership and organisational stewardship.
2.    Governance, financial and risk oversight expertise.
3.    Effective board leadership and facilitation.
4.    Political acumen, influence and relational leadership.
5.    Sharp analysis and sound judgment in complex and ambiguous environments.
6.    Diplomacy, negotiation and partnership capability.
7.    Ability to operate across diverse cultures and contexts.

Qualifications
Relevant qualifications in leadership and Company Directors Course and MBA or Bachelor of Commerce/Economics/Business Management/Political Science/Law degree or equivalent.

Attributes
  1. Strong commitment to The Fred Hollows Foundation’s vision and values. 
  2. Hong Kong residency preferred; experience in international or cross-cultural organisations desirable. 
  3. Mandarin language proficiency preferred but not essential.

Safeguarding
The Chair will be required to undertake training and sign up to the standards set for conduct by The Foundation, the Australian Government’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian NGO Co-operation Program and the Australian Council for International Development. This includes child protection and prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

Travel
Domestic and International travel may be required as part of this role.
Time Commitment 
  • Up to four Board meetings per year (two hours).
  • Up to one budget briefing per year (1-2 hours).
  • Up to two International Organisation meetings per year (1-2 hours).
  • Ongoing agenda setting and governance preparation.
  • Regular stakeholder engagement, including donor, partner and advocacy events.

Term of Appointment 
Appointed for an initial term of three years, renewable once by mutual agreement between FHF HK and The Foundation for a maximum term of 6 years. 

APPOINTMENT STRUCTURE
Board Director roles for The Foundation are voluntary (unpaid). The role offers the opportunity to contribute at a strategic level to a globally recognised organisation, shaping the growth of the Hong Kong market and enabling eye health programs that restore sight and transform lives and communities globally.

job.title: Communications and Outreach Assistant/Officer
job.description:
About WISE
We use programs on sports and movement to help improve teen girls’ interest and enthusiasm for being active, which results in them understanding their bodies better and growing in confidence and leadership. Although we use sports as a tool to teach our lessons, our goal is not for the students to become professional athletes. We believe that using movement and the life lessons we learn through sports - about how to take care of our bodies and our emotions - improves physical and mental health for many years to come. Most of our programs take place in Secondary Schools throughout Hong Kong, and we have the privilege of partnering with many wonderful organizations who provide volunteering and financial support throughout the year. For more information, visit www.wisewomenhk.org

About our Team
The WISE staff is a small team of dedicated individuals who work from a hybrid combination of our co-working space, their homes, and sometimes on-site at schools or events. Our Program team members often liaise directly with our schools, volunteers, and facilitators; and our Development and Communications positions often work with partners and donors, seeking ways to bring our mission to the public.

About the Position
We are hiring a part-time teammate (available to work minimum 3 days per week) who can work alongside our Communications and Outreach Assistant Manager to deliver effective communications that would raise the visibility and awareness of WISE (including our events and programs), while maintaining relationships with our community partners.

About You
We are seeking someone who is enthusiastic about our mission of empowering youth, women, and girls through sports. You need to be bilingual (fluent in spoken and written English and Chinese) and have 1 - 2 years of demonstrable achievement in one or more of the following areas: communications, marketing, digital design, community fundraising, event organising and general administration.

Timeline
Please note that applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and will be filled when the right candidate is identified, so we encourage you to apply early.

● Application deadline: 27 September 2026 at 11:59PM
● Interviews: conducted in late September - early October
● Start Date: October 2026

General Profile of the Communications and Outreach Assistant/Officer
You will report to our Communications and Outreach Assistant Manager and play an active role in increasing the visibility of WISE to the public in Hong Kong, as well as to garner stronger engagement with more people within Hong Kong, resulting in the support of WISE, monetarily and non-monetarily.

The priorities will be to:
● Content Creation & Graphic Design: Develop engaging written and multimedia content (social media assets, graphics, newsletters, and presentation collaterals) to showcase WISE’s school programs, events, and community impact.
● Channel Management: Assist in the content and community maintenance across WISE’s official platforms (Instagram, LinkedIn, and website).
● Programmatic Storytelling: Coordinate with internal teams to gather storytelling assets from school workshops for external communications.
● Campaign & Event Communications Support: Assist in delivering digital awareness campaigns and provide promotional, logistics, and on-site media support for WISE outreach events and workshops.
● Database & Asset Hygiene: Maintain the organization’s stakeholder contact databases, mailing lists, and digital asset archives to ensure accurate records.
● General Administrative Support: Provide ad hoc administrative support for ongoing organizational initiatives and partnership touchpoints.

Desired Skills & Experience:
● Strong verbal and written communication in both English and Chinese
● Familiar with digital communication channels (including Instagram and LinkedIn) and possess basic experience using web content management systems (CMS)
● Proficient in Canva, Google Workspace (G-Suite), and digital analytics tools
● Ability to self-manage with good time management and organizational skills
● Detail-oriented, proactive, adaptable, and eager to learn
● Able to work minimum 3 days per week
● Must have the right to work in Hong Kong

We offer a flexible and hybrid working environment. Salary will be commensurate with your experience and scheduled work days per week. More experienced candidates may be considered and offered the rank of Communications and Outreach Officer.

job.title: Fundraising Officer II - Events (2-year contract, renewable)
job.description:
Looking for a meaningful career that allows you to
make a difference in the world?

Join Oxfam Hong Kong, a member of the Oxfam confederation, in creating a world free of poverty. As an independent development and relief agency, we work with people living in poverty and partner organisations to implement effective development, humanitarian, policy advocacy, and public education programmes.

We are seeking passionate individuals to join our team and contribute to our poverty alleviation work. Join us and be part of the solution to end poverty and create a better world for all.

Fundraising Officer II - Events (2-year contract, renewable) [Ref.: FCU/FOII-E/26/01]

The Fundraising Officer II – Events is responsible for the implementation, evaluation, documentation and other post event follow ups of the fundraising events/activities delegated to her/him.

Responsibilities:
· To support and execute the development and implementation of the fundraising events/activities under his or her responsibility

· To recruit and service participants and volunteers
· To support the solicitation of sponsors and to service them thereafter
· To source for venues and propose the layouts
· To provide administrative and logistical support such as database management, receipting, printed materials, souvenir production, logistics arrangements, IT-related matters, and briefings for key stakeholders

· To take part and take turn to be secretary of the monthly Events Team meeting

· Able to meet tight deadlines and working under a roster, including working on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays as required
· Good customer service, interpersonal and organisational skills; detail oriented, work flexibly, creatively
· Experience in social media content creation, including video production and post writing, would be an advantage
· Good command of both spoken and written English and Chinese, and fluent Putonghua

Why Join Us
At Oxfam Hong Kong, our culture is shaped by our values, which reinforce what we care about and how we do things. Our five core values are: Justice, Empowerment, Inclusiveness, Accountability and Innovation. Learn more about Oxfam Hong Kong: https://www.oxfam.org.hk.

How to Apply
Closing date for application: 13 Oct 2026

Please send your application letter and resume, including current and expected salary and date of availability.
---
Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behavior at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us. Note: All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and may be subject to appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks.

(Data collected will only be used to process job applications. Applicants who are not invited for an interview within six weeks from the closing date can assume that their application was unsuccessful. Oxfam Hong Kong is an equal opportunities employer.

job.title: Intake Coordinator / Officer
job.description:
Asylum Services & Knowledge is a non-profit organisation that delivers legal and social services to refugees, asylum seekers and other displaced people in Hong Kong SAR. We work to support the vision of Hong Kong SAR as a welcoming and inclusive society. 

We provide free specialist legal help to people experiencing forced displacement, while offering tailored welfare and psychosocial support to those affected by trauma and destitution. Through strategic casework, research, training and technical assistance and community initiatives, we work to ensure that even the most marginalised members of Hong Kong society have equitable access to essential services and a voice in our society.  

Our engagement with the community aims to promote refugee participation in Hong Kong society. We are committed to creating a safe, supportive working environment, reflecting of the diverse communities we serve. For more information about Asylum Services & Knowledge, please visit www.ask.org.hk

Job Description and Person Specification
Job title
Intake Coordinator/Officer
Service
Direct Services
Reporting to
Director of Programmes
Salary
$14,098 – $24,225/month, commensurate with experience.
Work pattern
Full time, Monday – Friday, 9:30 am – 6pm (part time may be considered)
Duration
1 year
Purpose of position
The Intake Coordinator/Officer is the designated first point of contact for all prospective and returning clients, and their families and/or representatives. You work under the supervision of the Legal Services Manager and Director of Programmes to provide a responsive service to move clients through the registration and intake process to service delivery.

The position is responsible for the implementation of a coordinated and people-centred intake process that identifies client needs and facilitates prompt access to the full range of Asylum Services & Knowledge’s Direct Services, including Legal (USM), Legal (Detention), Welfare and Psychological. 

You will gain experience of client facing legal work under close supervision from our expert team of internationally qualified refugee lawyers, and alongside social welfare caseworkers and mental health experts. You will have the chance to learn more about and from refugees in Hong Kong, and to contribute to rewarding work assisting vulnerable migrants including refugees and asylum seekers in Hong Kong.

Depending on the successful candidate’s skills and experience, the role may be offered at either Coordinator or Officer level. Officer level candidates will be expected to exercise greater independence and judgement in conducting assessments, identifying needs and coordinating support.

Responsibilities
·       Work closely with the Direct Services team to provide information and assistance to clients, as needed during the intake process.
·      Assign, supervise, and review work related to coordination and intake by volunteers; and where no volunteers are available, to undertake such tasks. These include but are not limited to:
o  Responding to client enquiries through email, phone call, WhatsApp, drop-ins and any other forms of contact. 
o  Assessing clients’ needs and obtain accurate information and documentation to facilitate client intake, ensuring a responsive and people-centred approach to all client interactions. 
o  Arranging internal and external appointments, including coordinating schedules, reserving office space, and confirming appointments with all attendees. 
o  Liaise with interpreters, attend to interpreter matters, and keep an up-to-date records of interpreter details. 
o  Input, upkeep and coordinate data collection, entry, verification, monitoring and evaluation, ensuring legal and file management systems are accurate and up to date.   
·       Assist to determine clients’ eligibility for Asylum Services & Knowledge’s services and refer potential clients to alternative organisations, if required.
·       Undertake other administrative and organisational tasks, such as taking minutes, scanning, filing, and document management.  
·       Prepare, develop and deliver presentations and training to clients, partner organisations, pro bono lawyers, and others.
·       Contribute to maintaining positive working relationships with internal staff and with HKSAR government, professional bodies, UNHCR, NGOs and other stakeholders.
·       Keep up to date with legal and social welfare services available to clients, identify potential new services, and contribute to building the profile of Asylum Services & Knowledge.
·       Work in partnership with our Community Outreach team to maximise impact of our work and increase the scope for our clients to effectively contribute to the delivery of our legal services.
·       Attend all relevant staff meetings.
·       Comply with Asylum Services & Knowledge’s policies and procedures, and treat everyone with respect, dignity and fairness.
·       Perform other tasks as required for the support of the delivery of Direct Services, as requested by the Legal Services Manager and Director of Programmes. 

Requirements
Essential
·       Holder of a university degree in law or law conversion (LLB, LLM, JD or GDL), social work, human services or other relevant degree (industry experience may be considered in-lieu of professional qualifications). 
·       Multicultural sensitivity and ability to work with people from diverse backgrounds and across varying language barriers.
·       Good knowledge of domestic and/or international laws, processes and policies relating to refugees, asylum seekers and other forced migrants, and their application in practice, including judicial review.
·       Ability to respond proactively to clients’ needs while recognising when to seek assistance or refer for guidance.
·       Demonstrable commitment to upholding the principle of equal opportunities, and interest in issues related to refugees, asylum seekers and other forced migrants.
·       Fluency in verbal and written English, and ability to present complex information using simple and accessible language.
·       Highly self-motivated, with demonstrable organisational skills, and ability to work independently and under pressure.
·       Team-player with excellent interpersonal skills.
·       Experience of mentoring students, volunteers and/or staff.
·       Literacy in basic data entry, case management systems, Microsoft Office and Outlook.
·       Legal right to work in Hong Kong.

Desirable
·       Direct experience of forced displacement, or understanding of the challenges faced by refugees, asylum seekers and other forced migrants, including legal, mental health and social welfare issues.
·       Professional experience of working with vulnerable and young people who may be traumatised or distressed.
·       Experience of case-management or equivalent data gathering systems.
·       Experience of NGO service delivery and/or working with community organisations.
·       Ability to promote our work to a wide variety of external stakeholders, potential partners and community organisations.
·       Fluency in Cantonese.
·       Fluency in another language such as French, Arabic, Urdu, Hindi, Sinhala or Bengali would be a considerable asset.

Benefits 
·       Access to in depth training and supervision from internationally qualified lawyers.
·       Access to external professional development opportunities within the refugee response and forced displacement sector.
·       Flexible working hours.
·       Generous leave policy.

To assist us in processing your application for the role, please email the following to jobs@ask.org.hk with the subject line ‘Intake Caseworker/Officer’.
  1. A completed Application Form; and
  2. Your CV;
  3. Your Statement of Interest;
  4. Two writing samples (academic or professional; each over 500 words).
The closing date for applications is 5 October 2026. Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis.

job.title: Legal Officer
job.description:
Job Description and Person Specification

Job title Legal Officer
Service Legal Services
Reporting to Legal Services Manager
Salary HKD 25,200 per month
Work pattern Full time, Monday–Friday, 9:30am–6:00pm. Part-time arrangements may be considered.
Duration One year (with option to renew; performance and funding dependent)

Purpose of position
We are seeking a Legal Officer to join our team supporting refugees and people seeking protection in Hong Kong.

This is an exciting role offering frontline legal casework as well as opportunities for partnership-building and development. It is particularly suited to someone who wants to develop strong practical legal skills in refugee law, while gaining broader experience in how a community based organisation builds partnerships, mobilises resources and creates systemic impact.

Working under the supervision of the Legal Services Manager, you will assist clients in navigating Hong Kong's Unified Screening Mechanism. You will conduct client interviews, investigate complex factual and legal issues, work with experts and pro bono lawyers, and contribute to the preparation of high-quality legal submissions.

The role offers substantial exposure to refugee law, strategic litigation, pro bono partnerships, and complex stakeholder management.

Responsibilities

Legal casework
You will manage a caseload of matters, with appropriate supervision, and provide high-quality legal information and support to refugees and people seeking protection. Your work may include:

· Conducting client interviews and preparing detailed intake and case assessments;
· Supporting clients through the Unified Screening Mechanism and related legal aid and judicial review applications;
· Conducting legal research and detailed country-of-origin and factual research;
· Working with country experts, doctors, psychologists and other specialists to obtain evidence relevant to clients' claims;
· Drafting and contributing to witness statements, legal submissions, judicial review grounds and other legal documents;
· Identifying suitable work for pro bono lawyers, students, fellows and volunteers, and supervising and reviewing their written work;
· Providing constructive feedback and helping pro bono partners and junior team members develop their skills;
· Developing and delivering training and presentations for pro bono law firms, partner NGOs and other stakeholders; and
· Maintaining accurate and professional case records and coordinating the practical aspects of client representation, including appointments and interpreters.

Working across the organisation

As part of a small and collaborative team, you will:
· Build constructive relationships with colleagues and external stakeholders, including government bodies, the legal profession, UNHCR, NGOs and community organisations;
· Contribute to organisational events, training programmes and other initiatives;
· Participate actively in team meetings and organisational planning; and
· Uphold the organisation's policies and its commitment to treating clients, colleagues and partners with dignity, respect and fairness.

Person specification
We are looking for someone who combines strong analytical and writing skills with sound judgement, initiative and a genuine interest in refugee protection and human rights.

Essential
· A university degree, preferably in law or a related discipline;
· Excellent written and spoken English;
· Strong research, analytical and writing skills;
· Ability to communicate sensitively and professionally with people from diverse backgrounds;
· Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities;
· Careful attention to detail;
· Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a small team;
· Sound professional judgement and a willingness to take responsibility for your work; and
· Commitment to the organisation's mission and to high-quality, client-centred legal services.
· Right to work in Hong Kong

Desirable
We particularly welcome candidates with one or more of the following:
· Experience in refugee, immigration, or human rights law;
· Experience interviewing or working directly with clients;
· Experience in legal research and drafting;
· Experience working with law firms or pro bono lawyers;
· Experience in fundraising, partnerships, communications or stakeholder engagement;
· Knowledge of Hong Kong's Unified Screening Mechanism or judicial review process; and/or;
· Fluency in Cantonese or a language commonly spoken by refugee and migrant communities in Hong Kong.

job.title: Part-Time / On-Call Registered Social Worker
job.description:
The New Normal Charity Hong Kong is a registered Section 88 charity dedicated to supporting adults through life's most difficult moments. The organization focuses on making mental health and community resources accessible to individuals who may be facing financial hardship and emotional distress, in a city where many live in poverty and lack adequate support. It offers free peer-to-peer support groups, holistic well-being programs, and mental health-related training to ensure people receive timely and appropriate help. Guided by the belief that no one should face challenges alone, The New Normal Charity builds inclusive, compassionate support networks across Hong Kong.

Interested individuals and partners can connect with the organisation via hello@thenewnormalcharityhk.org.

The New Normal Charity Hong Kong is seeking a Part-Time / On-Call Registered Social Worker at the ASWO level to provide professional clinical backing for our peer support community.
 
We require a qualified professional to deliver expert safeguarding, triage and referral, and immediate crisis intervention when rare high-risk situations arise. This role ensures that while peer facilitators host our support groups, they have direct access to professional guidance to keep participants protected and appropriately cared for.
 
In this role, you will be on standby during nine evening peer support groups per month to provide remote intervention and guide facilitators. Beyond active group hours, you will conduct up to nine hours of post-group follow-up per month, completing intake assessments and connecting service users to other appropriate supports. You will also debrief facilitators following safeguarding incidents, maintain documentation, and collaborate with our Designated Safeguarding Lead to refine institutional policies and reporting.
 
Your Duties
On-Call Group Standby
Be on standby/on-call during our scheduled peer support groups (9 groups per month, 2.5 hours per group, total of 22.5 hours) to assist peer facilitators in handling safeguarding concerns, immediate crisis escalation or high-risk situations.
Our groups are scheduled on weekdays 7.30pm to 9.00pm. You would commence on call 30 minutes before doors open and remain available for 30 minutes after. Outside the standby window, volunteers follow TN's standing escalation protocol and there is no expectation that you will be contactable.

Risk Assessments and Crisis Intervention
Conduct immediate, professional risk assessments and crisis intervention remotely for service users who are identified as high risk during groups. Provide instructions to peer facilitators on group containment and emergency response.

Ad-Hoc Follow-up and Referrals: Provide time-limited follow-up to service users post-group. Maintain a referral network, conduct intakes and referrals to other services such as clinical psychologists, psychiatrists, or community mental health services (ordinarily up to 9 hours per month).

Facilitator Support and Documentation: Debrief with peer facilitators post-session when safeguarding concerns occur to ensure their well-being and safety. Maintain and update incident documentation on TN's systems and templates.
Incident Review, Audit and Enhancement: Support the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) and Head of Programmes to complete review and report of incidents to the Board, and enhance policy and service delivery. Perform other duties reasonably ancillary to the safeguarding function, such as training, protocol review and administration, as agreed with the Head of Programmes.

  • Professional Credentials: Must be a Registered Social Worker (RSW) in Hong Kong with a Bachelor's Degree in Social Work or above (ASWO equivalent qualification). Completed training in safeguarding, crisis intervention or suicide prevention.Willing and able to produce necessary certification/ documentation of qualification. Many people in Hong Kong struggle with life's challenges, often feeling isolated and uncertain about where to turn for help. By stepping into this role, you directly ensure that peer support remains a safe, sustainable space for over 1,000 people navigating life's most difficult moments in Hong Kong.
